details.claim: docs/prfaq-opencode-integration.md's FAQs (fork handling, restart, hook-mechanism comparison) and its bundled-plugin recommendation cite OpenCode's V1 plugin hook vocabulary as current: session.created/session.updated as returned-object keys, tool.execute.before with (input, output) args, and the async ({project, client, $, directory, worktree}) => Hooks factory shape, sourced from the stable opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ page.
details.corrected: opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ documents the V1 plugin API and still carries a 'New OpenCode v2 is now available' banner on the stable site. The anomalyco/opencode dev branch's migrate-v1.mdx states directly: 'V1 plugin implementations do not run in V2. Moving a file or renaming its config entry is not enough.' V2 replaces the hook-plugin surface entirely with Plugin.define({id, setup(ctx)}) and domain-scoped registration (ctx.tool.hook('execute.before', ...), ctx.session.hook(...), ctx.event.subscribe()). This was not a defect in either worker round -- the mission brief never asked for V1-vs-V2 currency verification on the plugin mechanism itself (only on the session.fork endpoint, which the document did correctly flag as dev-branch-only). The document's strategic thesis (bind a correlation-write to session lifecycle events, read by the unchanged git commit-msg hook) is portable to V2's ctx.session.hook/ctx.event.subscribe, but every concrete hook name and code sketch in FAQs 1-3 and the bundled-plugin recommendation targets V1 and will not run as written against a V2 install. The downstream Z-spec mission (m-2026-10-14-013) must not formalize V1 hook-name vocabulary without an explicit operator decision on which OpenCode version this integration targets, since V2 is still dev-branch, not a cut release.
